svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 1. Three observers of one encrypted conversation
svg.desc: The same conversation seen by three parties. The network path sees that you connected to a messaging service, when, for how long, and how much data moved. The provider sees whatever it chose to record, which varies enormously between services. The endpoint sees everything, because the message is decrypted there. A band below notes that the middle column is a design decision while the outer two are structural.
svg.text: Figure 1: Three Observers, One Encrypted Conversation
Module 2 asked this question about a page load. The same question, asked about a message, gives a different set of answers.
your provider, the network you are on

g.text: What it gets
That you connected to this service
Exactly when, and for how long
How much data moved, in each direction
The shape of it over time
What it does not get
Who you spoke to, or what you said.
Addressed by
Routing your traffic elsewhere, which is
the only thing that touches this column.
Structural. Every service has this.
What it gets
Whatever it decided to record.
One service answers a subpoena with two
timestamps. Another can supply an address
book, group memberships, and a target's
activity at fifteen minute intervals.
The important part
Both encrypt content with the same
protocol. The difference is not strength.
Addressed by
Choosing a different provider. Nothing in
the settings screen changes this.
What it gets
Everything. The message is decrypted there,
by design, because that is the point.
Which means
Encryption protects a message from
everybody except the person you chose to
send it to, and their device, and anybody
who later reaches that device.
Addressed by
Deciding who to talk to, and what to say.
Disappearing messages help against the
device later, and not against the person.

svg.text: Only the middle column is a choice.
The first and third are structural: any service has a network path, and any conversation has a recipient. The middle one was decided by whoever built the
service, and it is the only one where switching products makes a large difference. That is why Lesson 3.1 spent its time on what a provider retains.
Most advice about metadata is aimed at the middle column. Most of what identifies you in practice comes out of the first.
Figure 2 is about what somebody watching the first column can work out without ever reading a message.
